paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. Paul starts with one line for EVERYBODY: "Submit to one another out of reverence for Christ." (Ephesians 5:21). Then he speaks to wives, husbands, children, fathers, slaves and masters, and every group gets its own word. Nobody gets to sit back and just point at somebody else's section.

Now look at what sits underneath it all. Husbands are told to love "just as Christ loved the church and gave Himself up for her" (Ephesians 5:25). Fathers are told, "do not provoke your children to wrath" (Ephesians 6:4). Masters are told to "Give up your use of threats" (Ephesians 6:9). I think that's Paul saying the one with the most say has the most to give up. Every role in this passage points back to Christ, and none of them is about getting your own way.

And here's why it matters to you, baker. Slaves are told to serve "as to the Lord and not to men," because "the Lord will reward each one for whatever good he does, whether he is slave or free" (Ephesians 6:7-8). Masters are told that their Master is in heaven, and "there is no favoritism with Him" (Ephesians 6:9). So whatever your place is, at home, at work or anywhere else, the Lord sees what you do and how you do it. Do it as for Him, and no counter needs to get wiped twice when somebody walks in!
